units.fit_note: Also bans AI on assignments unless explicitly permitted (P06).

units.passage: however generative AI tools are not to be used on unit exams.
units.why: "generative AI tools are not to be used on unit exams" bans AI on exams, P22.

units.passage: This includes all assignments, papers, projects, exams, presentations, or any other graded component.
units.why: "This includes all assignments, papers, projects, exams, presentations" extends the ban to exams, P22.
units.fit_note: Exams are one item in a ban covering all graded work. Exams are one item in a list covering all graded work.

units.passage: Students shall not use AI tools during in-class examinations or assignments unless explicitly permitted and instructed to do so.
units.why: 'Students shall not use AI tools during in-class examinations or assignments unless explicitly permitted' bans AI in in-class assessment: P22.

units.passage: Students may use AI platforms to help prepare for cumulative assignments and project milestones (but not quizzes or QALMRIs).
units.policy: Students may use AI platforms to help prepare for cumulative assignments and project milestones, but not for quizzes or QALMRIs.
units.why: Allows AI for preparing cumulative assignments but excludes quizzes and QALMRIs; the quiz exclusion is the sharper rule (P22), the permission side is P14. I chose P22 for the exclusion.
units.fit_note: Quizzes and QALMRIs are the excluded graded items. Sentence mainly permits AI for preparing cumulative assignments and milestones; only the parenthetical bars quizzes and QALMRIs.

units.passage: Answering quiz or exam questions
units.policy: Using AI to answer quiz or exam questions is named as a potential misuse.
units.why: Listed as a potential misuse: AI "answering quiz or exam questions". Nearest is P22 (no AI on exams), though stated only as a concern.
units.fit_note: Framed as a concern about misuse, not a prohibition on exams.

units.passage: Tools such as Lockdown browsers with monitoring features may help deter misconduct.
units.why: Suggests lockdown browsers with monitoring to deter misconduct on online exams. Closed-device exam rules are P22; this is a tool suggestion, so P22 with a note.
units.fit_note: Coder A: Suggests proctoring tools to deter misconduct but does not ban AI on exams. | Coder B: Offered as an optional deterrent for online exams, not as a ban on AI in exams.

units.passage: Closed-book problem-solving exam in an introductory calculus course, proctored in person with no devices allowed.
units.why: The Level 0 examples are a proctored 'Closed-book problem-solving exam ... with no devices allowed', an in-person assessment with no AI: P22 (stated as an example, so informs).

units.passage: I did not consult other students' notes, the Internet, ChatGPT or any AI chatbot that could generate answers.
units.why: The student statement 'I did not consult other students' notes, the Internet, ChatGPT or any AI chatbot that could generate answers' is an attestation that no AI was used on an open-note quiz. P22 fits.
units.fit_note: Student pledge statement from Texas Tech.

units.passage: Reasonable measures taken to protect us from temptation are not antithetical to the Honor Code; thus, I reserve the option to proctor exams, provide multiple copies of exams for distribution, and restrict the technology tools students can possess while taking exams
units.why: 'I reserve the option to proctor exams, provide multiple copies of exams for distribution, and restrict the technology tools students can possess while taking exams' lets the instructor limit devices during exams, which covers AI-capable devices. P22 is the nearest type.
units.fit_note: Not AI-specific: restricts technology tools at exams generally. / Does not name AI; it covers device restrictions in exams generally.

units.passage: Students cannot give or receive aid on exams. This includes, but is not limited to, viewing the exams of others, sharing answers with others, and making unauthorized use of books, notes, AI, or the Internet while taking the exam
units.why: 'making unauthorized use of books, notes, AI, or the Internet while taking the exam' names AI explicitly among things not allowed on exams, so P22.
